thread:
eli_support: heads up — got a support ticket: customer says their monthly tokens were drained and reset earlier than expected. they were counting on reset at 2026-04-01 00:00 PDT but their account showed reset at 2026-04-01 07:00 UTC (which is 00:00 PDT) and tokens disappeared 1 hour before that — customer says they were charged for overflow.

eli_support: they claim 'tokens ran out ~2026-03-31T23:00:00-07:00' and then on the 1st they had 0 tokens for a full hour until the reset. seems like reset job ran on UTC boundary and we didn't apply local offset in time-of-day checks? might be DST related.

jamie_billing: can you paste account id and the exact timestamps from our billing API? I want to see what our service records as next_reset.

eli_support: account: acct_7f2b9 — customer TZ: America/Los_Angeles. From our logs: 
```
GET /v1/accounts/acct_7f2b9 -> {"id":"acct_7f2b9","quota":{"tokens_left":0},"next_reset":"2026-04-01T07:00:00Z"}
```
customer reported token depletion at `2026-03-31T23:00:00-07:00` (local). they expected next_reset at `2026-04-01T00:00:00-07:00`.

morgan_eng: quick note: biller service currently stores next_reset in UTC (ISO string) and we run the reset worker at 00:00 UTC for most accounts, except for accounts with custom timezone where we schedule offset. there was a change earlier this year to use the `tz` field from accounts table for per-account scheduling.

morgan_eng: i'm seeing a gap in the scheduler around DST transitions. if an account changed timezone earlier this month (or if we migrated their tz field) the cron job that generates the per-account reset at local midnight didn't update the precomputed `next_reset` until the nightly backfill. that means for a short window we fall back to the default UTC-run reset. this could make a reset appear earlier/later relative to local midnight.

nina_sre: do we have logs for the reset-worker run for acct_7f2b9 on 2026-04-01? need to confirm actual execution time.

deploy-bot: reset-worker: executing job run_id=rw-20260401-01 at 2026-04-01T07:00:10Z for account acct_7f2b9

morgan_eng: that matches `next_reset` (07:00Z). but customer says tokens dropped at 23:00 local — did they see an enforcement event earlier? maybe enforcement window checks `now >= next_reset - enforcement_delay` and enforcement_delay mis-calculated when DST offset changed.

eli_support: here's enforcement log snippet from gateway: 
```
2026-03-31T23:05:12-07:00 svc-gateway enforce_quota acct=acct_7f2b9 tokens_left=0 enforcement_reason=quota_exhausted
2026-03-31T23:05:13-07:00 svc-gateway rate_limit 429 account=acct_7f2b9
```
customer says they were blocked for ~60 minutes before the reset.

morgan_eng: aha — I see a bug: the gateway uses local-midnight calculation based on the `tz` field, but we recently started storing `tz` as an IANA name (e.g., America/Los_Angeles) and the gateway uses a naive `offset_hours` cached value instead of tz-aware conversion. DST change on 2026-03-14 (US) updated offsets but our cached offset didn't refresh for accounts that changed tz after the cache build. result: some accounts hit enforcement earlier by the delta (1 hour) until the sync ran.

jamie_billing: impact scope? how many accounts in america/* had tz changes or were migrated in the last 30 days? we need to know how many customers potentially saw early resets.

morgan_eng: running quick query now (repro): 
```
SELECT id FROM accounts
WHERE tz LIKE 'America/%'
AND updated_at > '2026-03-01'
AND tz_migration_pending = true;
```
(migrated accounts are marked `tz_migration_pending` until nightly job clears it)

morgan_eng: preliminary: ~12 accounts in prod matched. most low-volume but one enterprise tenant had high usage — probably the one who escalated.

nina_sre: mitigation steps? can we rollback the cache refresh to be tz-aware or force a one-off sync for affected accounts?

morgan_eng: immediate mitigation: force refresh of offset cache and recompute `next_reset` for affected accounts. I can run a safe backfill script to set `next_reset` = convert_to_utc(midnight_in_tz(account.tz), account.tz) for the next N days.

eli_support: we should also offer affected customers a manual credit top-up and apology. jamie, can billing do a 1:1 credit grant?

jamie_billing: yes we can. standard process: create a billing adjustment and mark reason `quota_reset_drift_dst`. we can use the admin API for manual top-up: 
```
POST /v1/admin/accounts/acct_7f2b9/credits
{ "amount_tokens": 50000, "reason": "quota_reset_drift_dst", "note": "manual grant after early enforcement; ticket #12345" }
```
we'll also add audit entry.

eli_support: i'll draft customer message: explain DST/cache bug, confirm we've backfilled their next_reset to 2026-05-01T07:00:00Z (UTC), and add 50k tokens while we patch.

nina_sre: long-term fix: migrate gateway to use IANA tz conversions (zoneinfo) not cached offset_hours. add unit tests around DST transitions, and add alert when enforcement_time_delta > 30m between gateway and billing service.

morgan_eng: i'll open a PR with the patch, plus a db migration to compute `next_reset_tz_aware` and re-run for all accounts. will do a staged rollout.

eli_support: thanks. for immediate action: jamie, please process the manual credit for acct_7f2b9 and leave the audit id here. morgan, run the backfill for the 12 accounts and ping when done. nina, add the alert to the observability board.

jamie_billing: done — audit_id=adj_20260401_89. credited 50000 tokens to acct_7f2b9.

morgan_eng: backfill complete for identified accounts. pushed patch to canary. will monitor.

eli_support: customer notified and accepted credits. closing on this thread but leaving notes for postmortem. :white_check_mark:

nina_sre: filing short postmortem and action items: 1) gateway tz fix, 2) billing/gateway delta alert, 3) run sweep for any accounts with `tz_migration_pending` older than 7 days.

eli_support: thanks team — good triage.
